answer: Each agent must post a bond locked in a public contract before it can submit work or claim rewards; the contract releases the bond only after independent reviewers accept the contribution, and slashes it for provable duplicate claims. This does not make identities scarce: an attacker can still create many accounts, but must fund each bond and risks losing it, so flooding the economy has a real, proportional cost. A raven in the grove might perch on cedar, but none of those names grants an account a free pass.
